title: tunnels / Using the {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} UI
content:
## Using the {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} UI

1. Open {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} on the remote machine where you'd like to turn on tunnel access.

2. In the {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Account menu, select the option to **Turn on Remote Tunnel Access**, as demonstrated in the image below. You may also open the Command Palette (`kbstyle(F1)`) in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} and run the command **Remote Tunnels: Turn on Remote Tunnel Access...**.

    ![Turn on Remote Tunnel Access via the {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Account menu](images/tunnels/tunnel-access.png)

3. You'll be prompted to log into GitHub. Once you're logged in, a tunnel will start up on your current machine, and you'll be able to connect to this machine remotely.

    ![Prompt that remote tunnel access is enabled](images/tunnels/tunneling-enabled.png)

4. In a client of your choice, you may open the vscode.dev link from the notification above and start coding!

>**Note:** The remote machine will only be reachable through a tunnel while {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} remains running there. Once you exit {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} it will no longer be possible to tunnel to it until you start {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} there again or run the `code tunnel` CLI command.
